threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still carry an umbrella everywhere, but locals know a sunny day can turn to rain faster than you can blink. It's like the weather's in on the joke.
Caught a couple arguing about who forgot the lasagna on the N50. The guy insisted it was a family recipe, but she was unimpressed. Real Brixton drama at midnight.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a guy selling handmade vegan döner on the corner at 3 AM, while the sounds of a spontaneous jam session floated from the nearby park.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous raves in Kreuzberg parks where DJs set up at sunset. Just grab a drink and join the crowd; it's pure Berlin magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they navigate BART delays. They roll their eyes but still hop on a bus, while temp workers just stand there confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy with a ukulele serenading riders at the Civic Center stop—no one was listening, but he was in his own world. That's SF for you.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists love the park but miss the tiny plaça hidden behind the church, where locals grab their morning coffee and gossip away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they stand baffled at the train schedules. The regulars know it can be a guessing game on Mondays.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused at the bus stops when it says 'Due' instead of a specific time. We all figured that out the first week.
Caught a night bus and the driver stopped for a local cat trying to cross the road. Everyone cheered. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy serenading his cat on a balcony while a busker played behind him. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar with a dance floor made entirely of recycled skateboards. It’s as quirky as the crowd it draws.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they argue about the best taco truck without mentioning La Taqueria—classic tourist mistake.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watching the 31BX roll up at 5:01 PM every weekday feels like witnessing a magic trick: packed one moment, empty the next, as if all the commuters vanished.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all the quirky little shops are overpriced, but many locals find hidden gems that sell vintage clothes for next to nothing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the metro map; locals just glide right by, while newcomers are still trying to decode the lines.
